title: Height-Balanced Tree Invariants for TypeScript AetherCast-LLM: Radio-Broadcasted Weight Streaming Enabling Memory-Free Edge LLM Inference
topic: AetherCast-LLM: Broadcasting AI Weights over Radio for Memory-Free Edge LLM Inference via RF

abstract: Edge devices often lack the DRAM capacity required to store full large-language-model (LLM) weight matrices. This work investigates a radio-broadcast streaming approach---AetherCast-LLM---where each weight row is transmitted as a packet, indexed in a balanced binary search tree, and applied to the input vector without ever materialising the complete matrix. We formalise the state machine that consumes packets, prove that the tree remains height-balanced and key-ordered after each insertion, and derive asymptotic bounds for packet lookup, insertion and output computation. Static analysis of the TypeScript implementation yields a structural complexity of $O(\log N)$ per packet and an AST profile of 187 source-lines across 14 functions. The results demonstrate that AetherCast-LLM can guarantee memory-free inference while preserving deterministic computational complexity. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/typescript-design-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261014_090117_aethercast_broadcasting_ai_weigh}
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
